clue.text: Report of a row, dispute? Mathematicians know all about this

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words that follow are to be spoken and matched by sound

parts.note: a row is a queue and a dispute is a tangle, giving 'a queue tangle' said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone reporting a quarrel in a line, with a learned aside about mathematicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' here is a line of people (a queue), not a quarrel, and 'dispute' is a tangle; spoken together they match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle of less than ninety degrees is basic geometry, a topic every mathematician knows thoroughly.

clue.text: Home with police turning up to get rebellious youth charged

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth rebel

explanation.surface: A rebellious youngster is charged after the police turn up at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy (Ted) was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes, a byword for delinquency.
explanation.definitionFit: To be indicted is to be formally accused of a crime, the same as charged.

clue.text: Lord eats odd bits of cake — not a hearty eater?

indicators.note: one word taking in another, as a diner swallows food, signals a container

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word are its odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: A nobleman nibbling cake, perhaps with a poor appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: someone who only pecks at food is a light eater.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who merely pecks at a meal, picking at morsels like a bird, is the opposite of a hearty eater.

clue.text: Chipper tots being heard

indicators.note: being heard means what is spoken stands for a word that sounds alike

parts.note: to tot up figures is to add them, so tots means adds

explanation.surface: Bright little children making themselves heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chipper' looks like cheerful and 'tots' like toddlers; in fact a chipper is a chipping tool and tots is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking tool used to chip away and shape timber, so it is a chipper.

clue.text: PM with cause to reform HP?

parts.note: Gordon Brown was a British Prime Minister

indicators.note: reform asks for the letters to be put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister with a cause to reform hire purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: HP looks like hire purchase, but HP Sauce is a well-known British brown condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: HP is a British brand of a brown, tangy condiment, an example of the type named.

clue.text: Diabolical comedian out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are not in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian whose fiendish act was out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniac means possessed by or like a demon, so devilish or diabolical.

clue.text: Politician caught in trick covers head

indicators.note: one thing caught in another is held inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: a wile is a trick or ruse
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician caught out in a trick hides their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers head' reads like a verb phrase, but it is a description: a garment that covers the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimple is a nun's cloth headdress covering the head, neck and sides of the face.

clue.text: Farm building that's neat inside?

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is a farm shed with cattle in it, not a tidy one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' suggests tidy, but it is an archaic word for cattle or oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, a farm building where cattle are housed.

clue.text: Prisoner, fragile person having a struggle

parts.note: con is short for convict
tender means delicate or easily hurt

explanation.surface: A frail inmate is having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is one who competes or contends, someone engaged in a struggle.

clue.text: Woman takes motorway into city

indicators.note: one piece going into another places it inside

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A woman drives a motorway into a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English cathedral city; the M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, its 1 read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Run gently with pet, crossing river

indicators.note: a piece crossing the river spans it, so it goes either side of the letter

parts.note: to pet is to stroke or tickle

explanation.surface: A gentle jog with a dog, wading over a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To trickle is to flow slowly in a thin stream, to run gently.

clue.text: In a short time band becomes wonderful!

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a wee is Scottish for a little while, as in 'bide a wee'
a hoop is a band or ring

explanation.surface: A band quickly turns out marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a short time' reads as 'soon', but it is the container and its outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of delight or excitement, cried out in celebration.

clue.text: Modify part of 'orse's equipment

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows a Cockney dropping the initial H, so the H goes from the tack word too

parts.note: a halter is a horse's headgear, part of its equipment

explanation.surface: Changing part of a horse's tack, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'orse imitates Cockney speech, which drops initial H, so the halter loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, the same as modify.

clue.text: Rebellious little princess ecstatic about boy

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, Princess of Wales

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it

parts.note: sent means transported with joy
Sid is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young princess thrilled about a lad, defying convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident opposes official policy, so as an adjective it means rebellious.

clue.text: Book Nine in academic citation

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a quote is a citation
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A book reference with a ninth item cited by a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel by Cervantes about a deluded knight is one of literature's great books.

clue.text: Fail to make progress in the current environment?

definitions.text: Fail to make progress in the current environment?

parts.words: Fail to make progress in the current environment?
parts.note: a swimmer staying upright in place amid the current is not going anywhere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current environment' sounds like the present state of affairs, but means a body of flowing liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay in place without advancing, as a swimmer does keeping afloat.

clue.text: Alien charged USA, spend being for a bit of Mexico

indicators.note: alien means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging

explanation.surface: A foreigner billed America, spending to buy part of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers all of 'charged USA spend'; 'being for' just links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1853 deal saw the United States buy a strip of territory from Mexico, now part of Arizona and New Mexico.

clue.text: Drink of the French — something that goes to the head

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

parts.words: something that goes to the head
parts.note: a bonnet is a hat, worn on the head

explanation.surface: A French drink that goes to your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to the head' suggests intoxication, but it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubonnet is a French wine-based aperitif, a brand of drink.

clue.text: Letter from a terrible ogre, beast

indicators.note: terrible implies the word is in a dreadful state, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an animal

explanation.surface: A note from a monstrous ogre and an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogram is a lightweight air-mail letter folded to form its own envelope.

clue.text: Film union thug's famous last words

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien
TU is a trade union
a brute is a violent thug

explanation.surface: A film union heavy's notorious final remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Caesar's dying reproach to Brutus in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare gives these words to Julius Caesar as he dies, the most famous dying words of all.

clue.text: Hard worker a bit upset the time after Christmas

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an ort is a scrap or leftover morsel
January follows December's Christmas; Jan is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A diligent worker feeling a bit low in the post-Christmas period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ort' is a crossword favourite for a scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is to labour tirelessly, so the word means a hard worker.

clue.text: Scrap paper's ending in hut

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a shed is a hut

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper ends up in a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap or small torn piece.

clue.text: Metal splinter twisted inside

indicators.note: the interior letters are given a twist, two of them changing places

parts.note: a sliver is a splinter

explanation.surface: A metal shard bent within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted inside' swaps the second and third letters of the splinter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element.

clue.text: Symbol of new life, new hope and love

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over in fresh order

parts.note: love is nothing in tennis, and nix means nothing

explanation.surface: An emblem of rebirth, fresh hope and affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' appears twice: the first belongs to the definition, the second rearranges 'hope'; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical bird rises reborn from its own ashes, an emblem of renewal.

clue.text: Two females at uni set up publicity

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the whole run reads from the bottom

parts.note: F is short for female, twice
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: Two female students mount a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a piece of exaggerated praise or promotion, publicity.

clue.text: City a VIP goes round, keeping record

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it within
going round means turning back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a nob is a toff or important person
a log is a record

explanation.surface: An important person tours a city while keeping a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes round' reads as touring, but it turns the VIP phrase back to front, and 'keeping' then holds the record inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a city in northern Italy.

clue.text: One can make endless incoherent noise!

definitions.text: One can make endless incoherent noise!

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: babel is a confused din of voices

explanation.surface: An infant capable of unending babbling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a baby is one who makes incoherent noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe, an infant, babbles meaninglessly before learning to talk.

clue.text: Celebrity eats Ryvita primarily — result is skeleton

indicators.note: one word taking in another, as a diner swallows food, signals a container

parts.note: fame is celebrity

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the initial letter

explanation.surface: A famous person living on crispbread wastes away to bones.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryvita is a British brand of rye crispbread, a diet staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame is a supporting structure, like the skeleton of a body or building.

clue.text: Army drifted — a particular corps might be found in a mess

definitions.text: might be found in a mess

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
blew means was carried along on the wind
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A military unit wandered off; one corps ends up in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is a military dining hall, not a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cutlery and dishes would be found in a mess, the place where service personnel eat.
